messages:
Rafa: Heads-up — spotted parity bug between node/python streaming clients. Python client sometimes merges two server-sent events into one when token refresh happens mid-event. anyone familiar?
Anya: oof. repro steps?
Rafa: run python sampleapp against local proxy, request a long streaming completion, force auth refresh by expiring token 1s into stream. client does refresh+reconnect. After reconnect the stream resumes but the first newline boundary gets trimmed and two events fold. Node client seems to handle this.
Rafa: sample log:
```
[python-sse] recv chunk: "data: {\"text\": \"hello\"}\n"
[python-sse] auth refresh, reconnect
[python-sse] recv chunk: "data: {\"text\": \" world\"}\n\ndata: {\"text\": \"final\"}\n"
[python-sse] parser emitted: "hello\n world" as single payload
```
Anya: interesting. do you use the same parser lib? python client uses a simple regex split on "\n\n" while node uses a stateful stream parser. regex can collapse boundaries when a leading \n is dropped.
SRE: also consider the token retry flow — are we sending a Range/Last-Event-ID header or re-requesting from scratch? If proxy returns 401 for the resumed request and client auto-retries without preserving the exact resume marker, server might send overlapping bytes.
Rafa: python code resumes by reconnecting and sending Last-Event-ID header. it then replays bytes from server; but our proxy returns a 200 for that resume and the model-router also streams a small prefix again. so python sees two events back-to-back but regex merges since the separator sequence is split across network chunks.
Anya: fix options: 1) make python parser stateful (buffer + search) like node, 2) normalize incoming chunks to ensure separators preserved, 3) add explicit "event_id" or seq field in payload so client can detect duplication/folding.
Infra-bot: model-router v1.8.0 deployed to staging @ 2026-03-20T18:03:02Z
Rafa: I prototyped 1) — switched python client to accumulate bytes and index-of "\n\n". simple patch fixes merging in my test.
Anya: can you paste the patch?
Rafa: snippet:
```
buf += incoming_bytes
while True:
  idx = buf.find(b"\n\n")
  if idx == -1: break
  evt = buf[:idx]
  buf = buf[idx+2:]
  handle_event(evt)
```
Anya: nice. also add a small unit test that simulates auth refresh by interleaving token-expire marker between bytes.
SRE: i'm worried about a race mode where python retries with exponential backoff and ends up requesting from an earlier Last-Event-ID due to clock skew; recommend server also include a short monotonic sequence header X-Chunk-Seq so clients can sanity-check ordering.
Rafa: added issue: https://git.internal/redwood/issues/6789 (add X-Chunk-Seq and server-side idempotency).
Anya: i'll update the python SDK to be stateful and add tests. can we also ensure docs mention that simple regex split is fragile?
Rafa: will add a note in sample-app README.
SRE: follow-ups: infra to confirm proxy resume behavior (infra-bot/marc), server to add optional seq header (model-router team), python SDK to switch to buffered parser (anya).
Infra-bot: noted — will audit streaming resume semantics across proxy versions.
Anya: thanks. PR incoming with tests and upgrade notes.
Rafa: thanks all, nice quick triage. will post CI results here. :rocket:
